title: Fault Lens: Forensics Panel for Failed Requests
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Design a single-pane 'Fault Lens' that lets engineers triage failed Redwood requests quickly and confidently from the Console. The panel should combine an error taxonomy summary, retry lineage, payload diff inspection, and suggested remediation steps into an actionable workflow.

Scope: prototype UI for Console request-level troubleshooting. Includes: (1) top-level failure cluster summary (heatmap by error class + rate change), (2) retry lineage timeline with interactive scrubber showing per-attempt latency and outcome, (3) payload inspector with side-by-side diff for inputs and outputs across retries, (4) automatic root-cause hints based on common signatures (e.g., token limit truncation, model OOM, kv-cache-miss), (5) exportable incident snapshot for SRE/Support.

Out of scope: backend routing changes, auto-rollbacks, or automated corrective actions — this ticket focuses on the UX surface and acceptance criteria for a working prototype that hooks to mocked data and the real request API later.

Design principles: minimize cognitive load, prioritize time-to-root-cause, make retry context explicit, surface both high-level trends and payload-level evidence, and provide clear next steps (replay, escalate, pin for evaluation).
acceptance_criteria: Top-level error taxonomy bar shows most frequent error classes for selected time window and links to filtered request list
Retry lineage timeline displays each attempt with duration, model variant, and outcome; clicking an attempt loads payload inspector
Payload inspector supports side-by-side comparison of request bodies and responses across two arbitrary attempts and highlights token-level diffs
Automatic root-cause hints show up when request signatures match known patterns (token-limit, truncation, model OOM, transform error) and link to documentation
Prototype contains export action that bundles timeline+payloads+notes into a downloadable incident snapshot (.zip) for support
comments: 2025-02-12 Sofia Martinez: Initial PRD and sketches uploaded to Figma. Focused on three-pane layout: (1) taxonomy/heatmap, (2) timeline, (3) payload inspector. Mock data implemented to emulate token truncation vs OOM signatures.
2025-02-14 Aisha Patel: Iteration: collapsed taxonomy to a compact pill-view when vertical space is constrained; added color scale accessible in high-contrast mode.

2025-02-15 Liam Chen (Eng): Feasibility note — payload diff is fine with current request sample size, but for >50KB payloads we should lazy-load and provide a truncated preview. Will add API contract for 'payload-snapshot' endpoint if design approved.

2025-02-17 Priya Nair (PM): Usability-testing plan added. Target: 5 platform engineers, tasks: identify root cause for token-limit vs model OOM within 5 minutes. Success metric: 80% completion rate without help.

2025-02-18 Design review: feedback to add an 'assume-failed-sequence' checkbox to show dependent downstream calls in service graphs; defer service-graph integration to follow-up ticket. Also requested copy edits for hint language to avoid prescriptive assertions (use probabilistic language: 'likely caused by').

2025-02-20 Aisha Patel: Prototype updated with diff-highlighting and download button; ready for dev handoff. Blocking: small API for payload snapshots and guidance on retention TTLs from infra (ENG-8503).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: embedding too many automated root-cause assertions increases false positives; current plan is to surface hints with confidence scores and link directly to logs and the original token stream for verification. We intentionally avoid automated remediation; the UX will recommend actions (replay with trimmed prompt, route to fallback model) rather than execute them automatically.
ux_flows: Open a request -> Fault Lens opens as right panel -> taxonomy highlights dominant error class -> click timeline attempt -> payload inspector shows side-by-side diff -> mark incident and export snapshot
prototype_notes: Prototype uses seeded examples across three failure modes: token-truncation (LLM truncates input), model-oom (server OOM), and user-input-parse-error. For each sample the UI demonstrates hint generation and the payload diff. Performance budget: initial render under 400ms with mocked data; large payloads lazy-load as compressed preview.
design_assets_status: Figma prototype v2 complete; accessibility pass scheduled; export icons and diff renderer component documented in handoff notes
